reason: The cited evidence (E1) states that LAM enables high cooling rates and temperature gradients, yielding refined microstructures for CoCrNi MEAs, which supports the first three premises. However, it provides no data on residual stress reduction, mechanical property improvement, or any results for AlCrFeNiSi, leaving the fourth and fifth premises unsupported by specific prior evidence.
premises: High-speed laser additive manufacturing (LAM) increases cooling rate and steepens thermal gradients.
Increased cooling rate and steep thermal gradients suppress elemental diffusion and dendritic segregation.
Suppressed segregation and reduced thermal gradients lower residual stress and defect formation.
A refined, homogeneous fine-grained microstructure enhances mechanical integrity (strength and ductility).
These LAM benefits observed in CoCrNi MEAs will transfer to cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi.
